scope: The twelve queued rows whose mediaPlan was source-required at 8df106dc4cb32fb288e68d5143ad80c202cafb05. This is an evidence ledger, not a publishing or code-adjudication override.
method: Read the original review decisions, searched exact names and primary-authority synonyms in English and relevant local-language terms, queried Commons metadata, and pixel-inspected downloaded candidates. Reusable means an explicit license was located, not that the photograph certifies the source-store code or package. Original rejections remain historical evidence. No image was generated, retouched, relabeled, or cropped to conceal a conflicting checkout label.

items.nextRequirement: The original page 5 source photograph, or an authoritative store listing that identifies the obscured apple and its complete code relationship, before selecting a cultivar-specific photo.

identitySources.supports: WSU identifies Rainier as its developed yellow/red-blushed cherry, including the historical white-cherry description. Ranier is treated as source spelling, not silently rewritten in the catalog.

photo.author: dnak (Dave Nakayama)
photo.pixelReview: Two sharply visible stemmed cherries have yellow-to-cream skins with red blush; more cherries are softly out of focus behind them. No brand, price, or checkout-code labels are present. Source metadata names Rainier cherries.

visibleIdentity.label: Rainier cherries
visibleIdentity.cue: Small round cherries with yellow skins and red blush, attached to slender green stems.

photo.claimBoundary: The exterior is not pure white. White is source/cherry-type language; a white interior is not visible. The competing label number 264497 is not cleared by this photo.

items.nextRequirement: Adjudicate 264497 versus 4260 from original store/source evidence. The reviewed photo alone cannot create a checkout-ready lesson.

photo.author: OttawaAC
photo.pixelReview: Whole spiny durians in yellow mesh bags fill a store display. A Frozen Durian sign and retailer price, bag labels, and barcodes are visible. Source explicitly describes frozen durian in a Canadian grocery store.
photo.allowedUse: Frozen whole-fruit context, not proof that the workbook listing is a flesh/segment package, and not a label-free recognition source. No source-store identity, unit, price, or code is copied.

items.nextRequirement: Capture the missing checkout code and confirm whether the source store's Frozen listing means whole fruit or packaged flesh. The prior helper's flesh/segments assumption is not source-recorded.

photo.author: Asit K. Ghosh (Thaumaturgist)
photo.pixelReview: Two raw vertically cut jackfruit halves on a dark background expose pale yellow flesh, white central cores, and large seeds inside green knobbly rinds. No labels or competing codes are visible.

visibleIdentity.label: Cut jackfruit
visibleIdentity.form: Large lengthwise-cut halves with knobbly rind
visibleIdentity.cue: The cut halves expose yellow flesh and large seeds around a pale central core inside a knobbly green rind.

photo.claimBoundary: The source identifies a photographed NS-1 specimen in Florida; that cultivar and origin must not be transferred to the workbook's unspecified cut-jackfruit listing.

items.nextRequirement: The original handwritten identity and missing numeric checkout code still require source-store evidence.

identitySources.supports: Guyana's Ministry of Agriculture identifies Buxton Spice as a leading mango cultivar with golden-yellow ripe skin.
NARI's annual report calls Spice a distinct popular mango variety; this strengthens the cultivar requirement and does not justify using unrelated mango cultivars.
The grower identifies its Buxton Spice tree and fruit and supplies an exact photograph. The page explicitly reserves all content/picture rights and asks users to contact it for permission.

attempts.query: Commons exact Spice mango, Buxton Spice, and mango plus spice
attempts.outcome: No exact freely reusable cultivar photograph found. Results are other named mango cultivars associated with Fruit and Spice Park, not Spice mango. Prior rejections remain.
Promising exact grower photograph, but All Rights Reserved. Not downloaded for publishing and not approved.

items.nextRequirement: A reusable photograph of the exact Spice listing, or a source-store photograph/label confirming a precise synonym, plus any necessary photo license. Do not replace it with Julie, Ataulfo, Kent, or a generic yellow mango.

items.preservedRejection: The original only result was a wild-onion flower, not a retail bulb.

attempts.author: Jon Sullivan
attempts.outcome: Pixel review confirms two clean loose brown/yellow onions without labels. This is a usable generic onion image but does not identify the unspecified color/type of the source 50lb listing or its exact bag. Retain as a lead, not exact-row approval.
Alternate source currently has GFDL 1.2 / CC BY-NC metadata and no machine-readable author. No new approval; the already-reviewed old rows are not changed by this lane.

items.nextRequirement: Source-store bag/label evidence specifying the onion identity and reconciling 724, 58312, and 63430. Medium and 50lb are not inferred from a loose bulb photo.

identitySources.supports: Jamaica's Agro-Investment Corporation associates Jamaican pumpkin with Calabaza and Cucurbita moschata, describing variable mottled green/yellow/buff fruit. Used only for category terminology, not the document's unrelated health or commercial claims.

The grower describes a diverse Jamaican Pumpkin population, C. moschata, also called West Indian Pumpkin or Calabaza. It does not establish that another named C. moschata cultivar is interchangeable with the workbook item.

attempts.author: Obsidian Soul
attempts.outcome: Pixel review confirms whole flattened mottled pumpkins and orange-fleshed cut pieces, but prominent foreign store labels include item number 000158, prices, weights, and barcodes. Reject for this 434 lesson; do not erase labels to make it pass. Philippine provenance also cannot establish a named Jamaican cultivar.
Metadata names Butternut, a distinct form; not an exact Jamaican pumpkin candidate.
Metadata describes a flower/vine and categorizes C. maxima; not the raw checkout fruit.
Public-domain USDA image is cooked/blended Haitian Soup Joumou, not raw pumpkin. Prior cooked-bowl rejection remains.

items.nextRequirement: A genuine reusable clean photograph of Jamaican/West Indian Calabaza fruit with no conflicting code label; Jamaican remains label-assisted unless exact cultivar/origin evidence is supplied. The alias research alone does not complete media admission.

photo.author: GIS Statia
photo.pixelReview: Two harvested sugar apples sit loose on pale paper, one green/yellow and one red/purple. Their segmented scale-like surfaces are clear; no brand, price, or code label is present. The photographer identifies sugar apples from Sint Eustatius.

visibleIdentity.label: Sweet sop (sugar apple)
visibleIdentity.form: Rounded fruit made of raised scale-like segments
visibleIdentity.cue: Raised scale-like segments divide the rounded surface; sweet sop can have green or red-purple skin.

photo.claimBoundary: The photographed origin and unspecified cultivars are not transferred to the workbook row. The seven-digit source value remains unclassified; do not truncate it, assume a public PLU, or borrow another Annona code.
